name: CA-03

key_factors: Bera holds a massive financial edge: $1.65 million on hand versus roughly $27,000 for Tucker
District leans Democratic by six points with a favorable national environment for the party

model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's Democratic lean, Bera's incumbency, and a lopsided cash advantage over an underfunded challenger, with markets pricing a Democratic win near 95 percent. A slight hedge toward the markets, rather than the pure fundamentals, accounts for the absence of polling in the race.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Bera or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow what is currently a one-sided contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ami Bera, a Democratic incumbent seeking another term in this Sacramento-area district, enters the general election as a clear favorite over Republican Robb Tucker. The district leans Democratic by six points, and the broader partisan environment adds to that edge. Bera has raised about $1.4 million and holds $1.65 million on hand, while Tucker has spent down to roughly $27,000 with almost no outside help on either side. Prediction markets put Bera's chances at 95 percent or better.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, campaign money, and market pricing. Those signals all point in the same direction: a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being how strongly the national House climate moves voters before Election Day.
